_what: The GRIGOLETTO inputs, measured. Four Notion pages (a design-system Blueprint, a 39-template Figma pack, an AI prompt kit and a course outline) arrived 2026-07-31. The Blueprint states rules; the template pack is the same author's shipped work. This measures the second against the first.
_why: The Blueprint is the best-written statement of design-system discipline to enter this programme, and it is PROSE - "cap your palette", "at most two typefaces", "snap everything to 8 points" - with nothing checking it. That is the entire thesis of this repository, arriving from outside it. Turning those rules into numbers is the only way to know whether they are a method or a mood.
_fairness: THE BLUEPRINT DOES NOT CLAIM THE TEMPLATES FOLLOW IT. They are separate products sold separately, and nothing in either says the pack is a worked example of the doc. Read what follows as "here is what the rules cost when applied to real shipped work", not as a contradiction caught.

The templates are HERO SHOWCASE PIECES - illustration-heavy single artboards (template 01 carries 497 VECTOR and 200 STAR nodes) - not component libraries. A rule about a design system's palette is not obviously a rule about a decorative illustration, and where that distinction matters it is drawn below rather than ignored.

corpus._why_not_all: Figma's free tier enforces a COST BUDGET, not a throttle: after roughly ten full-document reads it returned 429 with `x-figma-plan-tier: starter` and `retry-after: 399915` - 4.6 days. The remaining thirty are reachable, unread, and will be picked up when the window opens. Nine measured is nine measured; it is not "the pack".
corpus.reachability: Every one of the 39 is readable through the REST API with a personal token and NO duplication, even though the Figma MCP refuses them for want of edit access. That correction is written up in docs/REFERENCES.md.

first_pass_was_wrong._what: The first run of this measurement counted EVERY solid fill in the file and reported that all nine templates use flat #FFFFFF, between 71 and 661 times each.
first_pass_was_wrong._why_wrong: The rule is about the CANVAS - "replace every #FFFFFF with a warm off-white, and give the page background a subtle vertical gradient". A white highlight inside a vector illustration is not a page background. Counting it made a decorative choice look like a violated rule.
first_pass_was_wrong._what_the_right_subject_showed: Measured against artboard backgrounds instead, the rule LARGELY HOLDS. Only two of the nine use flat white on any artboard (01 on 3 of 14, 08 on 1 of 9). Templates 03 and 04 sit on #f8f7f8 - a warm off-white, which is the prescription almost exactly.
first_pass_was_wrong._lesson: The reading flipped from "nine of nine break this" to "seven of nine keep it" without a single byte of the subject changing. A measurement aimed at the wrong subject is not a weak measurement, it is a confident wrong answer.

typefaces.rule: "Choose exactly two typefaces - one expressive display serif and one neutral geometric sans - then delete every other font from the file."
typefaces._reading: Two of nine hold. The other seven carry three or four families, and the extra is usually a second grotesque doing the same job as the first (07 ships Funnel Sans AND Inter; 20 ships Inter AND General Sans Variable). That is the rule's own failure mode - not a deliberate third voice, but a font that arrived and never left.

canvas.rule: "Replace every #FFFFFF with a warm off-white (#FAFAF8) ... never flat white."
canvas._reading: Seven of nine hold at artboard level. See first_pass_was_wrong: this is the rule the first measurement got backwards.

eight_point.rule: "Define the scale - 8 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 - and use only those values for every gap and pad."
eight_point._reading: ZERO of nine hold, and this is the finding that does not soften on inspection. Measured only on auto-layout `itemSpacing` and `padding*` - numbers that are unambiguously spacing decisions, never a free-positioned illustration coordinate - off-grid rates run from 20% (05) to 98.5% (06, where 268 of 272 spacing values miss the scale). Template 03 declares no auto-layout spacing at all, so it is n/a rather than compliant: everything is free-positioned, which is the condition the rule exists to prevent.
eight_point._why_it_matters: This is the one rule of the three that a machine can check cheaply and completely, and it is the one nothing was checking. The Blueprint says the off-grid vibration is what "the viewer can't name but always feels as amateur"; the pack ships between one-in-five and virtually-all of its spacing off the scale. The gap is not disagreement about the rule, it is that a rule with no instrument is a preference.

type_scale.rule: "Size every piece of text from a single fixed scale instead of picking numbers by feel."
type_scale._not_judged: The Blueprint gives a scale for its own example system but states no maximum for anyone else's, so there is no threshold to fail against and none is invented here. REPORTED: the nine carry between 9 and 29 distinct font sizes (median 13). Template 03 uses 29 sizes across 1 typeface pair.

what_this_is_for: The Blueprint's rules map onto instruments this repository already has: the palette cap and the canvas rule are token-set questions (`vds figma pull` plus the variables manifest), and the 8-point rule is exactly the `geometry` proof kind - a count of surfaces that miss a declared shape, with a bound and a direction. Nothing here needs a new proof kind. It needs the rules written as bounds.
_what_this_is_not: A judgement on the templates as design. Off-grid spacing in a hero illustration may be the right call, and none of these numbers say the work is bad.
A measure of the pack. Nine of 39, stopped by a rate limit and not by a decision.

A check of the other four Blueprint rules (borders, shadows, motion, components), which the section headings promise and which were not measured because a static Figma document does not carry motion and because shadow discipline needs a threshold nobody stated.

vendored._why: blueprint.txt is the Blueprint page copied verbatim out of Notion. The digest is recorded so the source is pinned and any edit to it is visible. NOTE: it is a .txt and the em-dash gate only walks .js/.md/.html/.json, so this entry pins the evidence but does not currently exempt anything - the exemption was assumed and then checked, and the honest word is PINNED, not exempted. It would start exempting the moment the file were renamed to .md.
vendored._how: Fetched unauthenticated from Notion's own loadPageChunk API, paginated to exhaustion (225 blocks over 3 chunks). The page is public; no credential was used and none is needed.
vendored.derived_not_vendored: templates.json, measured.json and canvases.json are produced by this repository from the pack and carry no third-party prose, so they are under the house rules like any other authored file. The template NAMES in them are quoted exactly, minus the "NN " numbering prefix, which is presentation and is carried in the `n` field.
